newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Broke Russian energy firms may see assets transfer.
newsitem.headline: Broke Russian energy firms may see assets transfer.

text.p: The Russian government is considering transferring assets from one energy company to another to help firms resolve a nonpayments crisis, First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko said on Tuesday.
"One of the possible methods (for paying off existing debts) would be the transfer of property," Kiriyenko told a news briefing.
"For example, ownership of electricity stations belonging to RAO UES (Unified Energy System) could be handed to Gazprom.
Companies could also consider simply writing off their debts to each other, he said.
He put debts owed by electricity stations belonging to UES, Russia's dominant electricity supplier, to Gazprom, the natural gas monopoly, at around 35 trillion roubles ($6.1 billion).
The government will consider a programme for restructuring UES on July 3 but has promised not to break up the company. -- Mike Collett-White, Moscow Newsroom +7095 941 8520
